description: This line plot illustrates the relationship between initial confidence and three measures of accuracy—Final Accuracy, Δ Accuracy, and Initial Accuracy—for a model, likely an LLM, under varying conditions. The x-axis represents Initial Confidence, ranging from 0.86 to 1.00 in linear increments, with tick labels appearing approximately every 0.02. The y-axis represents Accuracy, scaled linearly from 0.0 to 1.0. The plot displays three distinct lines: the “Final Accuracy” is shown as a solid blue line with circular markers, starting at approximately 0.93 and remaining consistently high, above 0.95, across the entire range; the “Δ Accuracy” is depicted as a dashed brown line with diamond markers, beginning at about 0.25 and steadily declining to near 0.05 by the end of the x-axis; and the “Initial Accuracy” is represented by a dashed green line with square markers, starting at approximately 0.65, rising to a peak of about 0.88 near an initial confidence of 0.97, and then declining slightly to around 0.75.
